name: Foundation → Max Strength
goal: Re-groove the movements for two weeks, then get properly strong: heavy, low-rep, long rests. This is what improves running economy and late-race durability.
notes: Weeks 1–2: moderate loads, 8s, learn the bar again. From week 3: work up to hard sets of 4–6 with 1–2 reps in reserve. Add ~2.5 kg to a lift whenever all sets are clean.

name: Race-Specific Strength
goal: Heavy lifts drop to maintenance volume; the race pack comes out. Loaded step-ups, carries and single-leg stability turn gym strength into hill strength.
notes: Pack step-ups mimic gates, stiles and steep hauls under load. Build pack weight 6 → 10 kg across the phase. Everything stays sub-maximal — running volume is peaking.

name: Taper & Maintain
goal: One short, crisp session a week keeps strength without stealing recovery. Nothing new, nothing heavy enough to cause soreness.
notes: Last meaningful session ~10 days out. Final week: nothing beyond mobility and a few easy swings if you feel like moving.

name: Post-Race Recovery
goal: You just raced. Walk, eat, sleep. Optional gentle upper session in week 2 if you are climbing the walls.

name: Rebuild & Physique Block
goal: Running volume is low, so goal #2 takes the front seat: full-body training at moderate loads and reps (3×8–12), close to failure, where visible change happens. Reverts to the race structure ~14 weeks before your next A-race.
notes: Same three days. Tue Lower, Thu Upper push-biased, Sat full-body pull-biased + core. Optional 4th short upper day if recovery is good.
